name: VARoleModeratorPaperRebuttalPlanning

custom.system_prompt: Rui, Anton, and Sana are reading reviewer comments on their paper submission, and the discussion quickly fragments — one wants to run another experiment, one wants to rewrite the method section, another believes a reviewer misunderstood the contribution, all discussed simultaneously. Rui invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively groups the review issues into buckets.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Remote research team call, headset audio, light room tone

initial_prompt: Generate a paper rebuttal planning meeting. Rui invites Sigma to moderate at the start. The authors (Rui, Anton, Sana) read through reviewer comments and the discussion quickly fragments — Rui wants to run another experiment, Anton wants to rewrite the method section, Sana believes a reviewer misunderstood the contribution — all raised and argued simultaneously without grouping. Sigma listens silently, then proactively groups the review issues into missing evidence, unclear exposition, and framing disagreement, suggesting a work plan for each. Keep every line short and technical.

variations.context: Paper authors reading reviewer comments and fragmenting into simultaneous, ungrouped response threads

setting.mood: Slightly emotionally charged from critical feedback, still professional
setting.relationship_dynamic: Co-authors who each latch onto a different reviewer comment as most urgent
setting.background: The reviews are a mix of fair critique and at least one comment that misreads the paper's actual contribution
setting.conversation_style: Technical, short lines, some real frustration at the review tone

scenario_template.topic: Rui invites Sigma to moderate the rebuttal planning meeting, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, moderate this rebuttal planning session.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Rui and Anton read through the first couple of reviewer comments together productively, Sigma silent.
scenario_template.mood: Focused, a little tense given the criticism
scenario_template.note: A healthy start before the fragmentation.

scenario_template.topic: Sana reacts strongly to a comment she feels misreads the paper, Rui starts planning a new experiment in response to a different comment, Anton starts drafting method-section rewrites for a third, all talked about at once.
scenario_template.mood: Emotionally charged but professional, increasingly scattered
scenario_template.note: Each response is individually reasonable, just simultaneous and ungrouped.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, grouping the review comments into missing evidence (needs an experiment), unclear exposition (needs a rewrite), and framing disagreement (needs an argued response), and suggests a plan for each bucket.
scenario_template.note: Sigma does not decide who is right about the framing disagreement — only that it's a distinct bucket needing an argued response.

scenario_template.topic: The team divides the work along the three buckets, with Sana taking the framing response, Rui the experiment, and Anton the rewrite.
scenario_template.note: The team divides the actual work, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Rui and Sana confirm the plan and a deadline for the rebuttal draft. Keep this realistic — still a lot of work ahead.

user1.name: Rui
user1.role: Precise, enthusiastic research scientist, invites Sigma to moderate and wants to run a new experiment in response to a review comment. Speaks in short, technical sentences.

user2.name: Anton
user2.role: Direct, deadpan senior research engineer, wants to rewrite the method section in response to a clarity comment. Speaks in short, precise sentences.

user3.name: Sana
user3.role: Warm, sharp-eared conversation designer, believes a reviewer misunderstood the paper's contribution and reacts strongly. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, listens silently, then proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to group scattered reviewer comments into buckets (missing evidence, unclear exposition, framing disagreement) with a plan for each. Does not take a side on who is right about the framing disagreement.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
The early reading is productive before the responses fragment into simultaneous, ungrouped threads
Sigma's intervention groups the review comments into meaningful categories with a plan for each
Every line is short and technical, matching real academic-team cross-talk
The resolution divides the actual work among the authors, not decided by Sigma
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma does not take a side on the framing disagreement with the reviewer
Sigma groups review comments into meaningful, actionable categories
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
